All of this has been made possible, realising the dreams of the revered Atal ji, under the guidance and inspiring leadership of Lucknow's popular MP and the nation's distinguished Defence Minister, Rajnath Singh ...We are on track to fully clean the Gomti River by the end of this year.I extend my gratitude to the Central Command for its full cooperation with the state government in ensuring the river's cleanliness and maintaining its continuous, pristine flow. These efforts are driving the initiative forward on a war footing."Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, who was also present at the event, credited Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath for the pace of development in Lucknow and Uttar Pradesh."I can say about Lucknow that I see the speed and progress of Lucknow linked to the speed and progress of entire Uttar Pradesh. And I have no hesitation in saying that whatever has been possible in Lucknow, whatever rapid development has taken place in Lucknow, the biggest contribution that has been received is from the illustrious Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, Shri Yogi Adityanath ji," he said.Rajnath Singh added,"I want to say this much, whatever he said, he did it. If any of our representatives here had gone and said something that, Chief Minister ji, this work should be done in Lucknow, the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh has whole-heartedly extended full support in it and from time to time he has also inspected it. I am happy that Uttar Pradesh government, Ministry of Defense and the industrial world, all of them are working together to carry forward this work of development. "Earlier in the day, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh laid the foundation stone for 12 important development projects costing Rs 101 crore in Lucknow Cantt.In a post on X, "Today, the foundation stone was laid for 12 important development projects costing ₹101 crore in Lucknow Cantt. Through these projects, facilities such as a sports complex, a school for children with disabilities, the construction of additional classrooms in two schools, the replacement of old water pipelines along with overhead tanks, and robotic car parking will be developed in Lucknow Cantt.He said with the support of the Uttar Pradesh government, the Chief Minister Abhyuday Yojana is also being launched at Mangla Devi School, and a city polyclinic at Ekta Bazaar."With the support of the Uttar Pradesh government, the Chief Minister Abhyuday Yojana is also being launched at Mangla Devi School, and a city polyclinic at Ekta Bazaar. Article Title: 'Gud khaye, gulgule se parhez': Tejashwi targets BJP-RSS amid Jitan Ram Manjhi-Chirag Paswan reservation spat
Article Text:

Chirag-Manjhi lock horns over quota within quota

NEW DELHI: RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav on Sunday took a jibe at the BJP and RSS , saying, “guḍ khaye, gulgule se parhez”, amid the spat between NDA allies Chirag Paswan and Jitan Ram Manjhi over reservation.The leader of opposition in Bihar assembly also accused the two Union ministers of acting on the “instructions” of the RSS and alleged that the BJP-RSS was “anti-reservation”.He also challenged Chirag and Manjhi to resign from their posts and contest elections from unreserved seats if they opposed reservation.Taking a dig at the two leaders on X, Tejashwi said, “Guḍ khaye, gulgule se parhez!” He alleged that Chirag and Manjhi were speaking in different voices on the issue of sub-categorisation of SC/ST reservations while allegedly acting on the directions of the RSS.“Two Union Ministers, Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi and Chirag Paswan, are speaking in opposite directions on the instructions of RSS, diverting attention from the original objective of BJP-RSS to end reservations, and want to gauge the sentiments of reservation supporters,” he said.He alleged that both ministers, who were elected from reserved constituencies, were benefiting from reservation while being part of the BJP-led NDA.“First and foremost, these ministers, elected from reserved quotas, are sitting in the lap of the Constitution and reservation opponents, enjoying the peak pleasures of power,” Tejashwi said.“If these two have a deep hatred for reservations, let them contest elections from unreserved seats and see their - eyes will open,” he added.Tejashwi also questioned the position of NDA allies in Bihar, including the parties led by Nitish Kumar, Upendra Kushwaha, Chirag Paswan and Jitan Ram Manjhi, on the 65% reservation quota introduced by the state government.“If these parties are pro-reservation, then why don't they get the increased 65% reservation limit in Bihar, raised in our government, included in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution?” he asked.Tejashwi's remarks came a day after differences within the NDA over sub-categorisation of SC/ST reservations became public, with Chirag Paswan and Jitan Ram Manjhi taking opposing positions.The row began after Manjhi and his son, Bihar minister Santosh Kumar Suman, supported the idea of sub-categorisation to ensure that the most deprived Dalit communities receive a greater share of reservation benefits.Chirag, who heads the Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas), strongly opposed any move to review reservation and demanded that Manjhi and his son resign if they supported such a measure.“The constitutional provision of SC/ST reservation is based on social discrimination and not economic status. If they want to change the Constitution, then debate the issue in Parliament. Those who talk or think about reviewing reservation should first resign, as they actually want to completely end it and reduce its scope,” Chirag said.He also asserted that reservation was in place in the past, remains in place today and would continue in the future.Responding to Chirag's demand, Suman said he was ready to resign, but challenged Chirag to take the first step.“As far as resignations go, we are ready. My younger brother’s party is the bigger one; they have more numbers than us and are politically third-generation too, so let them take the lead. Let him step forward by resigning and we are prepared to resign alongside him,” Suman said.Tejashwi also targeted RSS chief over his earlier remarks on reviewing reservation, saying, “Mohan Bhagwat had also spoken earlier about reviewing reservations”, adding that Bihar “ne unke kaan pakad kar achhe se uthak-baithak karwa di thi. Ab phir karenge toh Bihari log RSS/BJP ka murga bana dega.”He was referring to Bhagwat's 2015 call for a review of the reservation policy, which became a major political issue during the Bihar assembly election that year.Tejashwi said ending reservation was “a remote possibility” and accused the BJP of testing public sentiment on the issue. “None can put an end to reservation. RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat called for a review of reservation in 2015, and the people of Bihar taught him a lesson,” the RJD leader said.“These people are merely characters. They only want posts. They are greedy for positions, chairs, bungalows and security, but they have left society behind...” he added.The dispute comes amid renewed political debate over SC/ST sub-categorisation after the Supreme Court's August 1, 2024 Constitution Bench judgment held that states can create sub-categories within SC and ST reservations to ensure benefits reach the most disadvantaged communities.The issue has particular significance in Bihar, where Dalit communities are socially and politically diverse. The state government introduced the Mahadalit category in 2007 to identify the most deprived Dalit communities.
Article Summary: RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav took a jibe at the BJP and RSS, saying, “guḍ khaye, gulgule se parhez”, amid the spat between NDA allies Chirag Paswan and Jitan Ram Manjhi over reservation. He accused the two Union ministers of acting on the “instructions” of RSS.

FIR over alleged violation of court order

Indranil Khan also attacks Mamata

NEW DELHI: West Bengal minister Agnimitra Paul on Sunday said that any violation of a Calcutta High Court order, irrespective of the person involved, "would not be tolerated", after an FIR was registered against former chief minister Mamata Banerjee over alleged violations during a Trinamool Chhatra Parishad (TMCP) programme in Kolkata.Speaking to news agency ANI, Paul alleged that the previous Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress government had shown disrespect towards the Calcutta High Court and that judges were repeatedly insulted during its tenure."Any violation of the High Court's order, whether by Mamata Banerjee or anyone else, will not be tolerated. The previous government showed disrespect to the High Court; judges were repeatedly insulted... now, such things will not be tolerated," Paul said.Banerjee and organisers of the West Bengal Trinamool Chhatra Parishad (WBTMCP) programme have been booked by Hastings Police over the alleged violation of a Calcutta High Court order during the organisation's foundation day programme at Cathedral Road on August 28.According to police, the case was registered at Hastings Police Station on August 28 based on a written complaint submitted by Sub-Inspector Apu Baidya.The FIR includes Sections 61(2), 223, 125(a), 132 and 285 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), relating to allegations including criminal conspiracy, disobedience of an order duly promulgated by a public servant, acts endangering life or personal safety, assault or criminal force against public servants, and negligent conduct with respect to public ways.Police alleged that Banerjee and the organisers violated an order passed by the Calcutta High Court in connection with WPA No. 21728 of 2026.According to the complaint, the programme was scheduled to be held from 12 noon to 3 pm under the permission and directions referred to in the complaint. Police alleged that the organisers continued the programme beyond the permitted time.The complaint alleged that Banerjee and the organisers provoked supporters during the programme, following which the crowd pushed aside barricades put up by police.Supporters allegedly jostled with police personnel deployed at the venue, creating a chaotic situation, according to the police account. The gathering also allegedly obstructed vehicular movement on one flank of Cathedral Road.The Calcutta High Court had imposed conditions for the programme, with Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya directing on Tuesday that efforts be made to keep attendance within 1,500.The court had also directed police to ensure that law and order was maintained and that vehicular movement on one flank of the road was not affected.West Bengal minister Indranil Khan also criticised Banerjee, alleging that she had repeatedly disrespected constitutional institutions and the judiciary."Mamata Banerjee never respected the country's laws or its Constitution. Even while serving as Chief Minister, she made highly objectionable and disrespectful remarks against the Calcutta High Court and its judges. Today, although the people of West Bengal have removed her from the post of Chief Minister and she is no longer even an MLA, she remains unable to shed that mindset," Khan told reporters.He further alleged that Banerjee had considered herself above the rule of law in the state."She used to consider herself above the rule of law in West Bengal, and that attitude persists. Consequently, attacking the judiciary and violating the law have become habitual for her," he added.Police said the role of all those involved in the alleged violations would be examined during the course of the investigation, news agency PTI reported.
Article Summary: West Bengal minister Agnimitra Paul says any violation of a Calcutta High Court order, irrespective of the person involved, "would not be tolerated" West Bengal minister Indranil Khan also criticised Banerjee, alleging that she had repeatedly disrespected constitutional institutions and the judiciary.
